Synopsis:
You find Astarion shirtless, tracing the scars on his back with his fingers, trying to read what they say through touch. Initially startled and a little embarrassed, he'll open up to anyone he thinks he can trust. An intimate moment, where he'll let characters with a high approval rating try to read what his scars say, or at least trace them into the dirt for him to read.

Cluster Contexts:
- CAMP_Astarion_CRD_ScarReading.json: Astarion is bare-backed and self-conscious, tracing deep, jagged scars carved into his skin by his former master, Cazador—scars he believes form a poem but cannot read himself. He can't easily see his own back (and his attempts to decipher the runes by touch have failed), so he only asks people he trusts—companions with high approval—to look or trace the letters for him. This scene typically plays out during quiet camp conversation or after an intimate night (it can follow the goblin-hunt celebration), and may come after the party has already learned, or been told, that Astarion is a vampire spawn. He’s embarrassed but sincere, and will open up to someone he thinks will treat the wound gently.
- CAMP_GoblinHuntCelebration_SD_ROM_NightWithAstarion.json: The scene follows the goblin‑hunt celebration after the Emerald Grove was saved: Astarion arranged a private tryst with the player that night, treating it like the practiced game of seduction and power he learned in Baldur’s Gate taverns. He fronts as self‑assured and teasing, but his usual script falters if the player refuses to play along — the examples show his mask cracking into real vulnerability. The next morning the player wakes to see him dressing and notices deliberate scars on his back carved by his old master Cazador; Astarion calls them a “poem” written in Infernal but can’t read them himself. Off‑screen, grove figures and revelers (Halsin, Nettie, other celebrants) are nearby and Halsin has already detected the player’s tadpole, so prior choices about the den and goblin camp shape who’s present and the atmosphere.
- LOW_CazadorsPalace_RitualRoom_PostCombat_OM_Astarion_AOM_COM_OOM.json: Astarion addresses a defeated Cazador after their fight. He pulls his former master from the coffin where he's recovering and has to decide what to do with him - kill him or carve the scars on Astarion's back into Cazador's and then use him as a sacrifice in the ritual.
- Astarion_Recruitment.json: Following a trail of whispered ADs ('Psst. Over here!' 'Come on, before it's too late!') we find a pale elf, hunched down near some long grass. He insists an intellect devourer (brain monster with legs) is hiding there, trying to cajole you to look and kill it. If you approach the grass, a boar bursts out - it was a distraction while Astarion got behind you. He's on edge, but pleased to have the jump on you. He holds a blade to your throat while demanding you tell him what happened on the ship. After a mind meld (vision where he sees a glimpse of your past) you can convince him that you're both victims and should work together to find an answer. Once he realises you're not a threat his tone changes from threatening to charming.
- LOW_CazadorsPalace_Crypt_PAD_CazadorsSkullComment.json: Player interacts with the skull in Cazador's dungeon and learn about Vellioth, Cazador's former master.Astarion makes a comment if he is nearby.

context: Astarion is bare‑back and self‑conscious, tracing deep, jagged scars carved into his skin by his former master Cazador; he believes the wounds form a poem in Infernal but cannot read them himself by touch. This is an intimate camp conversation—often occurring after a quiet night or a private tryst following the goblin‑hunt celebration—when he’ll only ask someone he trusts to look or trace the runes for him. The party may already know (or have just been told) that Astarion is a vampire spawn, and he’s sheepish about having that revealed by others (Raphael is mentioned in dialogue). Off‑screen, other revelers (Halsin, Nettie, etc.) may be nearby, and the player can offer to examine or trace the letters in the dirt; Astarion will reluctantly allow it only if he feels sufficient trust.
